## Compact Rules

### branch-pr

- Run `gh pr view --json` before creating to avoid duplicates
- Push branch first, then create PR with `gh pr create`
- Include issue references in body, not just title
- Never merge without review approval

### chained-pr

- Split PRs over 400 lines into stacked PRs with a base branch
- Each PR must be independently reviewable and buildable
- Document the chain order in PR descriptions
- Rebase stacked PRs after parent merges, never merge into child

### cognitive-doc-design

- Lead with decision/action, not background
- Progressive disclosure: headings first, details fold
- Never use "simply" or "just" — they hide complexity
- One concept per section, max 4 paragraphs per section

### comment-writer

- Start with observation before suggestion
- Use "We" not "You" to keep collaborative tone
- Never passive-aggressive phrasing; be direct but warm
- Link to relevant code/docs, don't just describe

### find-skills

- Search available skills by matching user intent to skill descriptions
- Surface installable skills with tradeoffs, not just a list
- Never recommend a skill without reading its SKILL.md first

### go-testing

- Use `go test -v -run` for focused runs, `-count=1` to bypass cache
- Prefer table-driven tests with `t.Run()` for subtests
- Golden files: store in `testdata/`, use `-update` flag
- Never use `os.Exit` in tests — use `t.Fatal` instead

### issue-creation

- Always search existing issues before creating (`gh issue list --search`)
- Include reproduction steps, expected vs actual behavior, and environment
- Use labels consistently; never create without at least one label
- Link related PRs/issues in body

### judgment-day

- Run dual review: one pass for correctness, one for style/patterns
- Fix confirmed issues before re-judging
- Don't flag subjective preferences as bugs — cite convention or spec
- Report with severity levels: blocking, should-fix, nice-to-have

### seo

- Always include title, meta description, and OG tags per page
- Use semantic HTML (main, nav, article, section) for crawl structure
- Add structured data (JSON-LD) for products, breadcrumbs, and FAQs
- Ensure all images have alt text and descriptive filenames
- Generate sitemap.xml and robots.txt; submit to Search Console

### skill-creator

- Frontmatter must include name, description (trigger-first, <250 chars), and license
- Activation Contract, Hard Rules, Decision Gates, Execution Steps, Output Contract required
- Keep body 180-450 tokens; move examples/schemas/edge cases to references/
- References must be local files relative to skill directory
- Hard rules must be observable; decision gates must cover real forks

### work-unit-commits

- Each commit = one reviewable unit: change + tests + docs if applicable
- Commit message: conventional commits format (feat:, fix:, refactor:, docs:)
- Never mix unrelated changes in one commit
- Amend before push if fix is small; new commit if work was already pushed
